heading: Kth Largest with a Min-Heap?
body:
Use a **min-heap of size k** to track the k largest elements.

Why min-heap? The root is the **smallest** of your k largest elements — that's exactly the kth largest overall. When you find a bigger element, evict the root (weakest of top-k) and insert the new one.

heading: When to Swap?
body:
**If heap has < k elements:** push the current element.

**If heap has k elements and current > root:** pop root, push current.

After processing all elements, `heap[0]` is your answer.

q: Why do we use a min-heap of size k instead of a max-heap to find the kth largest element?
options: A min-heap of size k keeps the k largest elements, with the smallest (kth largest) at the root for easy access
A max-heap would require O(n) space while a min-heap only needs O(k) space
Min-heaps are faster than max-heaps for insertion operations
A max-heap cannot be used to find the kth largest element
explain: A min-heap of size k maintains the k largest elements seen so far. The root is the smallest among these k elements, which is exactly the kth largest overall.
